[[File:Marta Vannucci.png|thumb|Vannucci in 2004]]
'''Marta Vannucci''' (10 May 1921 – São Paulo, 15 January 2021) was a Brazilian biologist and professor whose main research in biological oceanography was focused on [[mangrove]]s and [[plankton]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Morre Marta Vannucci, pioneira da oceanografia brasileira |url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/morre-marta-vannucci-pioneira-da-oceanografia-brasileira/ |access-date=31 May 2023 |website=revistapesquisa.fapesp.br |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Varela |first=Alex Gonçalves |date=1 December 2016 |title=Os textos da cientista Marta Vannucci sobre o plâncton no Instituto Oceanográfico da Universidade de São Paulo (1946–1969) |url=https://www.scielo.br/j/cpa/a/hSVbG5rgyygfnWqwJjhZrCq/?lang=pt |journal=Cadernos Pagu |issue=48 |language=pt |pages=e164810 |doi=10.1590/18094449201600480010 |issn=0104-8333|doi-access=free }}</ref> Marta was the first woman to become a full member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] and one of the precursors of [[oceanography]] in Brazil.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Marta Vannucci, a primeira mulher a se tornar membro da Academia Brasileira de Ciências – ABC |url=http://www.abc.org.br/2015/03/08/marta-vannucci-a-primeira-mulher-a-se-tornar-membro-da-academia-brasileira-de-ciencias/ |access-date=31 May 2023 |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Varela |first=Alex Gonçalves |date=2012 |title=GÊNERO E TRAJETÓRIA CIENTÍFICA: AS ATIVIDADES DA CIENTISTA MARTA VANNUCCI NO INSTITUTO OCEANOGRÁFICO DA UNIVERSIDADE DE SÃO PAULO (1946–1969) |url=https://periodicos.uff.br/revistagenero/article/view/31181 |journal=Revista Gênero |language=pt |volume=13 |issue=1 |doi=10.22409/rg.v13i1.536 |doi-broken-date=12 July 2025 |issn=2316-1108|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Marta was born in [[Florence]], Italy and moved to Brazil with her family when she was still a child in 1927. Her father was a medical doctor and surgeon and a Full Professor at the [[University of Padua|University of Pádua]] and the [[University of Florence]]. The Vannucci family was a rich and traditional family who left Italy after the fascism ascension. In Brazil, her father worked as a surgeon at the {{Interlanguage link|Hospital Matarazzo|lt=Hospital Matarazzo|pt|https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospital_Umberto_I}}. Marta had a lot of contact with Brazilian scientists due to his father's job.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=28 November 2016 |title=Academia Brasileira de Ciências |url=http://www.abc.org.br/article.php3?id_article=4057 |access-date=1 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161128135016/http://www.abc.org.br/article.php3?id_article=4057 |archive-date=28 November 2016 }}</ref>

== Career ==
She studied at the [[Colegio Dante Alighieri|Colégio Dante Alighieri]] and the [[University of São Paulo]].<ref name=":0" /> She earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1944 and continued working as an assistant for [[Ernst Marcus (zoologist)|Ernst Marcus]], a professor at the Zoology Department, until 1950.

Marta was invited to be part of the Instituto Paulista de Oceanografia, the first institute of oceanography research in Brazil, which was part of the Agriculture Department.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Histórico – IOUSP |url=https://www.io.usp.br/index.php/institucional/historico.html |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=www.io.usp.br}}</ref> Together with [[Wladimir Besnard]], who was the institute director, they shared the views that the institute should focus more than just fishing but on oceanographic science research in general. That is why they worked to get the institute incorporated into the University of São Paulo. The entire process happened in nine months, and the institute was renamed Instituto Oceanográfico, becoming a research institute at the University of São Paulo in 1951.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" />

Under the knowledge and influence of [[Wladimir Besnard]], who was studying in [[Cananéia]], a region rich in mangroves, Marta had an opportunity to specialise in mangrove ecosystems.<ref name=":0" /> In 1956, Marta earned a scholarship from [[UNESCO]] to research at the University of Marine Biological Station Millport, having the opportunity to visit other research centres in Scotland and learn techniques to study plankton.<ref name=":0" />

She became the first woman director of the Instituto Oceanográfico in 1964.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> During her management, she organised post-graduate courses, started the construction of the institute building at the University of São Paulo, and negotiated the purchase and followed the construction of the first Brazilian oceanography research ship, which was named to honour the institute's first director, Wladimir Besnard.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pesquisadores do mar |url=https://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/pesquisadores-do-mar/ |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=revistapesquisa.fapesp.br |language=pt-br}}</ref> And in 1966, she was the first woman to become a full member of the Brazilian Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":3" />

From 1969 to 1971, she worked for UNESCO at the Indian Ocean Biological Centre at Cochin in India as a curator of the international Indian Ocean expedition plankton collections.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Condolences |url=http://mangrove.or.jp/english/subpage/condolences.html |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=mangrove.or.jp}}</ref> She moved to Mexico in 1972 to work at the Universidad Autónoma de México and returned to India in 1974 as the UNESCO director regional officer in Delhi. From 1982 to 1990, she became the chief technical advisor of UNDP/UNESCO programmes on mangroves in the Asian and Pacific regions.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 July 2019 |title=Marta Vannucci – DK Printworld (P) Ltd. |url=https://dkprintworld.com/author-book/marta-vannucci/ |access-date=7 June 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 1989, Marta published a book about the relationship of humans and mangroves for non-specialists called "The Mangroves and Us: a synthesis of Insights." The first Portuguese edition of the book was published in 1999.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Varela |first=Alex Gonçalves |date=23 March 2020 |title="Uma dádiva das marés": os estudos sobre manguezais da cientista Marta Vannucci em sua trajetória internacional, 1969–1989 |journal=História, Ciências, Saúde-Manguinhos |language=pt |volume=27 |issue=1 |pages=115–132 |doi=10.1590/S0104-59702020000100007 |pmid=32215521 |s2cid=216197301 |issn=0104-5970|doi-access=free }}</ref> For 15 years, Marta was invited by Dr Shigeyuki Baba to teach a mangrove course to international students in Japan. Through this work, she had the chance to contribute to a collaborative publication of a world mangrove atlas.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Osborne |first=Daphne J. |date=September 1998 |title=SPALDING, M. D., BLASCO, F. & FIELD, C.D. (eds) 1997. ''World mangrove atlas''. International Society for Mangrove Ecosystems, Okinawa 903-01, Japan. 178 pp. ISBN 4-906584-03-9. Price US$ 60.00 (hardback). |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1017/s0266467498300528 |journal=Journal of Tropical Ecology |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=723–724 |doi=10.1017/s0266467498300528 |s2cid=83742724 |issn=0266-4674|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From 1990 to 1999, Marta was the vice president of the International Society for Mangrove Ecosystems, becoming the acting President in 1999 and, in the following year, an Honorary adviser for the Society.<ref name=":5" />

In 1997, she received, from the Brazilian President, the Grand Cross of the Order of Scientific Merit.<ref name=":5" />

Marta became internationally known for her work in biological oceanography, with over 100 published scientific papers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Martha Vannucci – ABC |url=https://www.abc.org.br/en/membro/marta-vannucci/ |access-date=7 June 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> Many scientists who knew Marta would call her "Mother of Mangroves".<ref name=":5" />

Marta retired from UNESCO in 1989.<ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
Marta got married twice and had two sons, Érico and Dino.<ref name=":2" /> During an interview with the Brazilian Academy of Sciences, she stated it "is actually difficult to reconcile the life of a wife and mother with that of a scientist".<ref name=":3" />

Marta died on 15 January 2021 in São Paulo at 99 years old.<ref name=":2" />
